findings.title: allowedIss issuer validation bypassed by an array-valued iss claim (loose any-match)
findings.evidence: validateClaimValues() at src/verifier.js:159 accepts a claim whenever ANY payload value matches ANY allowed matcher (`values.some(v => allowed.some(a => a.test(v)))`). This function is used for the single-valued `iss` validator registered at lines 474-476, which passes no `array` flag. The validator's `array` flag is consumed only to choose an error string in validateClaimType (lines 144-152) and is never enforced, so nothing rejects an `iss` array. Data flow: verify() decodes the token (line 281) and calls verifyToken() (line 310/352); decoder.js accepts a JSON object payload containing an array claim; in the validator loop value = payload['iss'], arrayValue = true, values = the array (lines 210-212); validateClaimType at line 221 passes because every element is a string; then line 226 calls validateClaimValues, and the loose `some` at line 159 lets a token with iss = ['https://attacker-domain/', 'https://valid-iss'] satisfy `allowedIss: 'https://valid-iss'`. An attacker reaches this by submitting a signed JWT whose payload carries that array. In deployments that derive the verification key from payload.iss (e.g. get-jwks with providerDiscovery, as in the advisory PoC), the attacker's own domain is used to fetch the attacker's public key, so the attacker-signed token verifies and issuer spoofing/auth bypass results (CVE-2025-30144 / GHSA-gm45-q3v2-6cf8). The upstream fix changed this path to require `values.every(...)` for non-array claims and to route genuinely-array claims (`aud`) through a separate any-match helper.
